doc.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020

title: First records bought at twelve; Don Fagerquist and the Dave Pell Octet
summary: Shew names the three albums he bought, the first jazz trumpeter he heard, Don Fagerquist, and later taking his chair with Dave Pell.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well Bobby, this has been great. I’m so glad that you could get together with me this afternoon. And I’m going to wrap up by testing your memory. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
At the age of twelve I believe you broke your piggy bank so you could buy three records. And do you remember what those three records were?
Dave Brubeck’s first album on Fantasy Records, “Stan Getz with Strings,” and a J.J. Johnson album.

I was so blown away. And I never heard a trumpet player yet, not a jazz player. Well I had heard Harry James on a 78 but not realizing you know. But the first jazz trumpet player I heard was Don Fagerquist with the Les Brown band. And I went uh — what the heck is that? You know? And then I started buying all the Les Brown albums so I could listen to Don. And then years later when he was with the Dave Pell Octet I bought all of those. And then after Don had passed away, Dave called me up. I took Don’s chair in the Dave Pell Octet.
